notes: Archived (retrieved 2026-11-14). Searched bone, muscle and radiation using the public OSDR Search API (cgene), including all result pages. Selected two description-evidence-reviewed drafts per topic, preferring explicit flight context and clear topic titles, then numeric accession; sorted by numeric accession. Radiation studies include ground-based exposures and simulated deep space radiation, not astronaut flight measurements. Every study page returned HTTP 200. Drafts describe study questions, not inferred results. API documentation: https://api.nasa.gov/

items.text: Scientists compared muscle gene activity in mice that flew on a space shuttle with mice that stayed on Earth.
items.studyTitle: Effects of spaceflight on murine skeletal muscle gene expression

items.text: Scientists compared genes and chemicals in thigh muscles from mice in space and mice on Earth.
items.studyTitle: Gene-metabolite network linked to inhibited bioenergetics in association with spaceflight induced loss of quadriceps muscle

items.text: Scientists tested ways to protect muscle and bone in mice sent to the International Space Station.
items.studyTitle: Targeting myostatin/activin A protects against skeletal muscle and bone loss during spaceflight [plasma proteomics]

items.text: Scientists studied how radiation exposure affected chemical processes in the spleens of mice.
items.studyTitle: Effects of low dose space radiation exposures on the splenic metabolome

items.text: Scientists tested skin cells from 15 kinds of mice with simulated deep space radiation.
items.studyTitle: Coalescence of DNA double strand breaks induced by galactic cosmic radiation is modulated by genetics in 15 inbred strains of mice

items.text: Scientists studied how spaceflight affects the healing of broken bones.
items.studyTitle: Gene-metabolite networks associated with impediment of bone fracture repair in spaceflight
